source_text: Hoc autem in praesentiarum duabus ex causis accidit; quia et sententia Manichaeorum de criminum est probata consiliis, et excitae persecutionum procellae inopes spiritus a veritatis favore deterrent.
pass_a_gloss: But this happens for the present from two causes; because both the sentence of the Manichaeans has been approved from the counsels of charges, and the stirred storms of persecutions deter poor spirits from the favor of truth.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil

pass_b_english: At present this happens for two reasons: the Manichaeans’ position has won approval in councils of wrongdoing, and the storms of persecution that have been stirred up frighten feeble spirits away from favoring truth.

choices.why: Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
